title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Measures for Handling Official Documents of the People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Circular on Issuing the Measures for the Handling of Official Documents of People's Courts

Fa Fa [2012] No. 22

To all local people's courts at various levels, military courts at various levels, railway transportation intermediate courts and basic-level courts, maritime courts, and people's courts at various levels in the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Measures for the Handling of Official Documents of People's Courts are hereby issued for your compliance and implementation.

November 16, 2012

Measures for the Handling of Official Documents of People's Courts

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Measures are formulated with reference to the Regulations on the Handling of Official Documents of Party and Government Organs and in light of the actual work of people's courts, for the purpose of promoting the scientific, institutionalized, and standardized handling of official documents of people's courts, and improving the quality and efficiency of document handling.

Article 2 These Measures apply to the handling of official documents in people's courts at all levels.

Article 3 Official documents of people's courts (including electronic documents and fax telegrams) are official instruments formed in the course of trial enforcement and judicial administration work, which have specific legal effect and standardized formats. They are important tools for conveying and implementing the Party's line, principles, and policies, executing national laws, issuing judicial interpretations, guiding, deploying, and consulting on work, making requests and answering questions, and reporting, notifying, and exchanging information.

Article 4 The handling of official documents refers to a series of interrelated and sequentially connected tasks, including the drafting, processing, and management of official documents.

Article 5 The handling of official documents shall adhere to the principles of seeking truth from facts, accuracy and standardization, conciseness and efficiency, and security and confidentiality.

Article 6 The General Offices (Offices) of people's courts at all levels shall be responsible for the handling of official documents within their respective courts, and shall provide professional guidance and supervision to the document handling work of lower-level people's courts.

Article 7 People's courts at all levels shall attach great importance to the handling of official documents, strengthen organizational leadership, enhance team building, establish confidential document departments, or assign dedicated personnel to be responsible for document handling. Confidential document staff shall be dedicated to their duties, maintain confidentiality, be meticulous in their work, and possess the corresponding professional knowledge of law and secretarial work.

Article 8 Modern office methods shall be fully utilized in the handling of official documents to continuously improve work efficiency.

Chapter II Types of Official Documents

Article 9 The main types of official documents of people's courts are as follows:

(1) Resolution. Used for major decision-making matters discussed and adopted at meetings.
(2) Decision. Used for making decisions and deployments on important matters, and for rewarding or punishing relevant units and personnel.
(3) Order (Decree). Used for approving the awarding and promotion of ranks, and for commending relevant units and personnel.
(4) Announcement. Used for announcing important matters or statutory matters to the public at home and abroad.
(5) Circular. Used for publishing matters that need to be complied with or made known within a certain scope.
(6) Opinion. Used for presenting views and handling methods on important issues.
(7) Notice. Used for issuing and conveying matters that require lower-level people's courts and relevant units to handle, be informed of, or implement; for appointing and removing judicial personnel; and for approving, forwarding, or transmitting official documents.
(8) Bulletin. Used for commending advanced individuals, criticizing mistakes, conveying important guiding principles, and informing important situations.
(9) Report. Used for reporting work, reflecting situations, and responding to inquiries to the People's Congress at the same level and its Standing Committee, or to higher-level authorities.
(10) Request for Instructions. Used for seeking instructions and approval from higher-level authorities.
(11) Official Reply. Used for replying to matters requested for instruction by lower-level people's courts.
(12) Proposal. Used for people's courts at all levels to submit matters for deliberation to the People's Congress at the same level or its Standing Committee in accordance with legal procedures.
(13) Letter. Used for consulting on work, asking and answering questions, requesting approval, and replying to approval matters between people's courts, or between a people's court and other organs not under its jurisdiction.
(14) Minutes. Used for recording the main circumstances and decisions of meetings.

Chapter III Format of Official Documents

Article 10 Official documents of people's courts generally consist of the following components: copy number, classification level and duration of confidentiality, urgency level, issuing authority identifier, document number, signatory, title, primary addressee, main text, description of attachments, signature of issuing authority, date of issuance, seal, notes, attachments, carbon copy addressees, printing authority and date, and page numbers.

(1) Copy Number. The serial number of the printed copies of the document. Classified documents shall indicate the copy number.
(2) Classification Level and Duration of Confidentiality. The classification level and duration of confidentiality of the document. Classified documents shall be marked as "Top Secret," "Classified," or "Confidential" according to the degree of classification, along with the duration of confidentiality.
(3) Urgency Level. The time limit requirements for delivery and processing of the document. According to the degree of urgency, urgent documents shall be marked as "Most Urgent" or "Urgent," and telegrams shall be marked as "Most Immediate," "Urgent," "Routine," or "Deferred."
(4) Issuing Authority Identifier. Composed of the full name or standardized abbreviation of the issuing authority plus the word "Document" (文件). Alternatively, the full name or standardized abbreviation of the issuing authority may be used alone. When documents are issued jointly, the identifiers of all joint issuing authorities may be used together, or the identifier of the lead authority may be used alone. When the identifiers of joint issuing authorities are used together, they shall be arranged in a standardized order, or the identifier of the lead authority shall be placed first.
(5) Document Number. Composed of the abbreviation for the issuing authority, the year, and the sequential number of issuance. When documents are issued jointly, the document number of the lead authority shall be used.
(6) Signatory. Documents submitted to higher authorities shall indicate the name of the signatory.
(7) Title. Composed of the name of the issuing authority, the subject matter, and the document type. For normative documents adopted at meetings, the name of the meeting and the date of adoption shall be indicated below the title and above the main text.
(8) Primary Addressee. The main recipient of the document, which shall use the full name, standardized abbreviation, or a unified term for similar types of organs.
(9) Main Text. The main body of the document, used to express its content.
(10) Description of Attachments. The serial numbers and names of the attachments to the document. If a document has attachments, the serial numbers and names of the attachments shall be indicated after the main text and before the date of issuance. Approved, forwarded, or transmitted documents and their accompanying comments are part of the main text and shall not be treated as attachments.
(11) Signature of Issuing Authority. The full name or standardized abbreviation of the issuing authority. When documents are issued jointly, and the identifier of the lead authority is used alone, the signatures of the issuing authorities shall be arranged in a standardized order, or the lead authority's signature shall be placed first. When the identifiers of joint issuing authorities are used together, the order of signatures shall be consistent with the order of the identifiers.
(12) Date of Issuance. The date when the document was adopted at a meeting or signed by the responsible person of the issuing authority. For jointly issued documents, it is the date when the responsible person of the last issuing authority signed. For telegrams, the date of dispatch shall prevail.
(13) Seal. If an issuing authority is named on the document, the seal of that authority shall be affixed, and it shall correspond to the named authority. For joint downward documents, all joint issuing authorities shall affix their official seals.
(14) Notes. Matters that need further explanation, such as the scope of distribution and transmission of the document, shall be indicated in parentheses.
(15) Attachments. Explanatory, supplementary, or reference materials for the main text of the document.
(16) Carbon Copy Addressees. Other organs that need to execute or be informed of the content of the document in addition to the primary addressee. Their full names, standardized abbreviations, or unified terms for similar types of organs shall be used.
(17) Printing Authority and Date. The authority that prints the document and the date of printing.
(18) Page Numbers. Sequential numbers indicating the pages of the document.

Article 11 Chinese characters, numbers, foreign language characters, units of measurement, and punctuation marks used in official documents shall comply with relevant national standards and regulations. Official documents of people's courts in ethnic autonomous areas may use both Chinese characters and the local minority languages.

Article 12 The paper size for official documents shall be international standard A4. The paper size for special types of official documents shall be determined according to actual needs.

Article 13 The layout of official documents of people's courts shall comply with the national standard Format of Official Documents of Party and Government Organs (党政机关公文格式).

Article 14 The main layouts and their scope of application for official documents of people's courts are as follows:

(1) "Party Group of [Name of People's Court]." Used by the Party Group of a People's Court to submit requests and reports to higher authorities, and for appointments and removals of cadres.
(2) "Document of [Name of People's Court]." Used by a People's Court to convey and implement the Party's and State's guiding principles, policies, or important work deployments, and to issue important decisions, notices, etc.
(3) "[Name of People's Court]." Used by a People's Court to submit requests and reports to higher authorities, reward or punish relevant units and personnel, issue notices and bulletins, and consult with relevant units on work matters.
(4) "General Office (Office) Document of [Name of People's Court]." Used by the General Office (Office) of the Supreme People's Court or Higher People's Courts, upon authorization, to convey or issue important normative matters on behalf of the court.
(5) "General Office (Office) of [Name of People's Court]." Used by the General Office (Office) of a People's Court to submit requests and reports, issue notices and bulletins on work matters, and consult with relevant departments of other units, ask and answer questions.
(6) "Minutes of the [Name] Meeting of [Name of People's Court]." Used by a People's Court to record the main circumstances and decisions of a meeting.
(7) Official documents issued by internal departments of a People's Court generally use the letterhead of the court's own stationery.

Chapter IV Rules for Document Transmission

Article 15 The transmission of documents shall be necessary, practical, and focused on relevance and operability.

Article 16 The relationship governing the transmission of documents of a people's court shall be determined based on its jurisdiction and the scope of its functions and powers. Generally, documents shall not skip levels of authority. In special circumstances requiring skipping a level, the skipped authority shall be simultaneously copied.

(1) People's courts may transmit documents between superior and subordinate levels, and with other organs at the same level.
(2) The General Office (Office) of a people's court may, upon authorization, transmit documents to lower-level people's courts and other organs; other internal departments shall not directly transmit documents to lower-level people's courts or other organs.
(3) Internal departments of a people's court may transmit documents to other departments within the same court within their respective scopes of functions and powers; they may transmit documents with counterpart departments in superior or subordinate people's courts; and they may transmit documents with relevant departments of other organs at the same level.
(4) A people's court and other organs at the same level, or the General Office (Office) of a people's court and the General Office (Office) of other organs at the same level, may jointly issue documents when necessary. For jointly issued documents, the lead department shall be clearly identified.

Article 17 The following rules shall be observed when transmitting documents to higher authorities:

(1) In principle, the document shall be addressed to a single higher authority, and a copy may be sent simultaneously to relevant higher authorities and authorities at the same level, but not to lower-level authorities.
(2) For matters on which a lower-level authority has requested instructions, if it is necessary to submit a request for instructions to a higher authority in the name of the present court, a proposed opinion shall be formed before submission, and the original text from the lower-level authority shall not be forwarded.
(3) A request for instructions shall be limited to a single matter. Requested instructions shall not be embedded in reports or other types of documents that are not requests for instructions.
(4) Except for matters directly assigned by the responsible person of the higher authority, no official document shall be submitted to an individual responsible person of a higher authority in the name of the present court, nor shall any document be submitted to a higher authority in the name of an individual responsible person of the present court.

Article 18 The following rules shall be observed when transmitting documents to lower-level authorities:

(1) In principle, the document shall be addressed to the recipient authority, and a copy may be sent to relevant authorities as needed. For important documents, a copy shall be simultaneously sent to the direct higher authority of the issuing authority.
(2) If a matter involves the functions and powers of multiple departments within a people's court, and the departments have not reached consensus through consultation, no document on the matter shall be issued downward.

Chapter V Drafting of Official Documents

Article 19 The drafting of official documents includes the procedures of drafting, reviewing, and signing.

Article 20 The drafting of official documents shall achieve the following:

(1) Adhere to the Party's line, principles, and policies, comply with the provisions of the Constitution and laws, follow the fundamental laws of justice, and accurately reflect the guiding ideology of the people's court's work, as well as the decision-making intentions and work requirements of the Party Group of the Court.
(2) Proceed from reality in all matters, conduct in-depth investigation and research, fully demonstrate, extensively solicit opinions, analyze issues realistically, and ensure that the proposed policies, measures, and methods are practical and feasible.
(3) The content shall be concise, the theme prominent, the viewpoint clear, the structure rigorous, the expression accurate, and the wording refined.
(4) The document type shall be correct, the format standardized, and the classification level appropriately assigned.
(5) If the document involves matters within the functions and powers of other organs or departments, the drafting department must solicit opinions from the relevant organs or departments and strive to reach consensus.

Article 21 Before submitting to the court leadership for signing, a draft of an official document issued in the name of a people's court or a draft issued in the name of the General Office (Office) on behalf of the court shall be reviewed. The focus of the review is:

(1) Whether the reason for issuing the document is sufficient and the basis for issuance is accurate.
(2) Whether the content complies with national laws, administrative regulations, relevant central policies, and the relevant provisions of the present court; whether it is consistent with other existing relevant documents; and whether the proposed measures and methods are practical and feasible.
(3) Whether matters involving other units have been coordinated and consensus has been reached.
(4) Whether the document type, document format, etc., comply with the relevant provisions of these Measures and the national standard Format of Official Documents of Party and Government Organs.

Article 22 A draft document that is deemed unsuitable for issuance after review shall be returned to the drafting unit with an explanation of the reasons. If the conditions for issuance are met but the content requires further research and revision, the drafting unit shall revise it and resubmit it.

Article 23 Signing of Official Documents:

(1) Official documents issued in the name of the Party Group of the Court shall be signed by the Secretary of the Party Group, or by a Deputy Secretary of the Party Group authorized by the Secretary.
(2) Important documents or documents of a comprehensive nature issued in the name of the Court shall be signed by the President of the Court, or by a Vice President authorized by the President. Other documents issued in the name of the Court shall be signed by the Vice President in charge of the relevant area.
(3) Documents issued in the name of the General Office (Office) on behalf of the Court shall be signed by the court leadership, or, with the consent of the court leadership, by the Director of the General Office (Office).
(4) Other documents issued in the name of the General Office (Office) shall be signed by the Director of the General Office (Office) or, upon authorization, by a Deputy Director. For important documents, if the Director of the General Office (Office) deems it necessary to submit them to the court leadership for approval, approval shall be obtained before signing.
(5) For documents issued by internal departments concerning their respective work, they shall be signed by the head of the department. For important documents, they shall be submitted to the Vice President in charge for signing.
(6) Minutes shall be signed by the leader who presided over the meeting.
(7) For jointly issued documents, they shall be countersigned by the responsible persons of all joint issuing authorities.
(8) When signing a document, the signatory shall indicate their opinion, name, and date. Circling or signing one's name on the document shall be deemed as agreement.

Chapter VI Processing of Official Documents

Article 24 The processing of official documents includes the processing of incoming documents, the processing of outgoing documents, and arranging and archiving.

Article 25 Main Procedures for Processing Incoming Documents:

(1) Receipt and Signing. Incoming documents shall be checked item by item, signed or stamped after verification, and the time of receipt shall be noted.
(2) Registration. The main information of the incoming document and the status of its processing shall be recorded in detail.
(3) Preliminary Review. Incoming documents shall be subject to a preliminary review. The focus of the preliminary review is: whether the matter should be handled by the present court; whether it complies with the rules for document transmission; whether the document type and format meet the requirements; whether matters involving the functions and powers of other departments have been coordinated and countersigned; and whether it meets other requirements for document drafting. Any document that fails to meet the requirements after preliminary review shall be promptly returned to the originating unit with an explanation of the reasons.
(4) Proposal for Handling and Approval. Informational documents shall be distributed after determining the scope of recipients based on their content, requirements, and work needs. Documents requiring executive action shall have proposed handling opinions prepared based on their content and nature, to be submitted to the court leadership for approval, or be directly forwarded to the relevant department for processing. If two or more departments are required for processing, the lead department shall be clearly identified. For urgent documents, a specific time limit for processing shall be clearly indicated.
(5) Undertaking Processing. The department undertaking the processing shall handle the assigned document promptly. If a clear processing time limit is specified, the processing shall be completed within that limit. For matters within the scope of its functions and powers, the undertaking department shall provide a clear opinion. For matters involving the scope of business of other departments, it shall actively consult with those departments, jointly formulate a clear opinion, and submit it to the Vice President in charge for approval. If the matter is not within the department's scope of functions and powers, it shall promptly explain this to the court leadership that approved the assignment. If directly assigned by the General Office (Office), the document shall be promptly returned to the assigning General Office (Office) with an explanation of the reasons.
(6) Circulation for Reading. Documents shall be promptly sent to the circulation list for reading or approval by the intended recipients, based on the leadership's instructions and work needs. When circulating documents for reading, the location of the documents shall be monitored at all times to prevent omissions, misdirection, or delays.
(7) Follow-up and Urging. The General Office (Office) of the People's Court shall promptly understand and grasp the processing progress of documents and urge the undertaking departments to complete processing on time. Urgent documents shall have designated personnel responsible for tracking and urging. For important issued documents, the General Office (Office) of the People's Court shall promptly understand and provide feedback on the implementation status.
(8) Response. For documents requiring a reply, the processing progress and results shall be promptly reported to the originating unit, and relevant units shall be informed as needed.

Article 26 Main Procedures for Processing Outgoing Documents:

(1) Review. Before printing, documents that have been signed and approved by the responsible person of the People's Court shall undergo a review by the General Office (Office) and the undertaking department concerning the approval procedures, content, document type, classification level, format, and attachment materials. If substantive modifications are required, the document shall be resubmitted to the original signatory for review.
(2) Registration. After review, the document number, distribution scope, and number of copies to be printed shall be determined and recorded in detail.
(3) Proofreading. Before formal printing of the document, the final proof of the document shall be proofread.
(4) Printing. The printing of documents must ensure quality and timeliness. Classified documents shall be printed in locations that meet confidentiality requirements. Top-secret documents shall be handled by designated personnel.
(5) Issuance. After printing is complete, the document's text, format, and print quality shall be checked before distribution.

Article 27 Classified documents shall be transmitted through confidential transportation channels, postal confidential communication services, urban confidential document exchange stations, or by designated confidential document personnel of the sending and receiving authorities. They shall be transmitted via encrypted telegrams or computer information systems that comply with national confidentiality regulations.

Article 28 After the processing of an official document is completed, it shall be promptly filed and archived in accordance with the Archival Law of the People's Republic of China, the Implementing Regulations of the Archival Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Provisions on Archival Work of People's Courts. Telegrams shall be filed and archived together with the relevant documents.

For official documents jointly processed by a People's Court and other organs, the original document shall be filed and archived by the lead authority. Other organs shall retain copies or other forms of the document's copy.

Chapter VII Management of Official Documents

Article 29 People's courts at all levels shall establish and improve management systems for official documents to ensure strict and standardized management and to fully utilize the effectiveness of official documents.

Article 30 Official documents of people's courts shall be managed uniformly by the confidential document department or by designated personnel. People's courts at all levels shall establish confidential document rooms and confidential reading rooms, and shall equip them with appropriate staff and necessary security and confidentiality facilities in accordance with relevant confidentiality regulations.

Article 31 Before the classification level of a document is determined, confidentiality measures shall be taken in accordance with the proposed classification level. After the classification level is determined, strict management shall be carried out according to the designated classification level. Top-secret documents shall be managed by designated personnel.

The official documents whose confidentiality period has expired shall be declassified on their own. If the classification level of an official document needs to be changed or lifted, the original authority that determined the classification level or its superior authority shall decide.

Article 32 The scope of distribution of official documents of the People's Courts shall be implemented in accordance with the requirements of the issuing authority; if changes are necessary, approval from the issuing authority shall be obtained.

Before classified official documents are made public, a declassification procedure shall be completed. The time, form, and channel of public release shall be determined by the issuing authority.

Official documents approved for public release shall have the same effect as official documents formally issued by the issuing authority.

Article 33 Reproduction and compilation of confidential-class and secret-class official documents shall comply with relevant regulations and be approved by the leadership of the court. Top-secret official documents shall generally not be reproduced or compiled; if there is an actual work need, approval from the issuing authority or its superior authority shall be obtained. Reproduced or compiled official documents shall be managed as originals.

A reproduction copy shall be stamped with the seal of the reproducing authority. A reprint copy shall indicate the name of the reprinting authority and the date. The classification level of a compilation shall be marked according to the highest classification level of the documents included therein.

Article 34 The revocation and abrogation of official documents shall be decided by the issuing authority, the superior authority, or the competent authority in accordance with their scope of authority and relevant laws and regulations. If an official document is revoked, it shall be deemed invalid from the beginning; if an official document is abrogated, it shall be deemed invalid from the date of abrogation.

Article 35 Classified official documents shall be returned or destroyed in accordance with the requirements of the issuing authority and relevant regulations.

Article 36 Official documents that do not have archiving or preservation value may be destroyed after approval. The destruction of classified official documents must strictly follow the relevant regulations for approval and registration procedures to ensure no loss or omission. Individuals shall not privately destroy or retain classified official documents.

Article 37 When an authority is merged, all official documents shall be merged and managed accordingly; when an authority is dissolved, official documents that need to be archived shall be organized and transferred to the archival management department in accordance with relevant regulations.

When a staff member leaves or resigns, the authority where they work shall urge them to transfer or return any temporarily stored or borrowed official documents in accordance with relevant regulations.

Chapter VIII Supplementary Provisions

Article 38 Litigation documents, judicial interpretations, and other specific legal official documents of the People's Courts shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations.

Article 39 Official documents concerning foreign affairs shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the competent foreign affairs authorities.

Article 40 Specific measures for handling electronic official documents shall be formulated separately.

Article 41 These Measures shall be interpreted by the General Office of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 42 These Measures shall come into effect as of January 1, 2013. The "Measures for the Handling of Official Documents of the People's Courts" (Fa Fa [1996] No. 9) issued by the Supreme People's Court on April 9, 1996 shall be simultaneously abolished.
